name: South Point Hotel Casino and Spa

reviews.title: South Point Adventure!
reviews.text: We didn’t stay at South Point but went to play Bingo. We’ve been to other places to play Bingo but it’s not the same.We also enjoy the variety of Slot Machines there as well.

reviews.title: First Visit At South Point
reviews.text: Fleew in for two days to celebrate my Mom's 70th bday. I was warned this hotel is far down the strip, but you know that is totally ok with me. I arrived and we greeted by Concierge asking if I needed help, I thanked them and said no, my Mom was coming down to get me. Hotel is super clean can tell that the staff really care about where they work. Lots of smiles, there wasn't any elements of that guests, or issues going on with over drinking. The bathroom is spacious, especially if someone has a walker, or wheelchair. Larger mini fridge for all your drinks and treats. There was team penning going on, which I loved seeing the full equestrian area. Probably more amenities than I saw. This hotel is wonderful with easy access to the strip via Lyft or Uber. I enjoyed my few days at South Point, will definitely be back.

reviews.title: Best Ever
reviews.text: Been going there since it opened in 2005!, clean, so much to do and best food ever!! Just got back tonight. Will be there again soon!

reviews.title: Awesome experience
reviews.text: Hotel is amazing.  Wear comfortable shoes.  I was getting 10,000 steps a day  just walking around the casino floor.  So much to see and do. Movie theater ,bowling ,bingo, pool and sp much more.  Rooms are super clean and BIG.  Most comfortable bed I've ever slept in.   The only bad thing was on my second day, security knocked on my door doing a wellness check.  I didn't like this.  They claimed I haven't left the room in 3 days.  I was out of my room a ton without the do not disturb sign off.  I had housekeeping in the day before, so I don't know.  I think front desk should have called first.  Anyway still 10/10 and I highly recommend.

reviews.title: this has got to be the busiest place in all of vegas.....
reviews.text: just like what vegas used to be--affordable--never saw so much action in vegas--they have $5 table games also--free valet parking with a tip-- $1.50 hot dogs--reasonable buffet--after midnight really cheap meals--if you stay here they have free shuttles to the airport which is only 5 miles away--we were really impressed.....

reviews.title: Fantastic stay, with no downside
reviews.text: My wife and I just returned home to Ireland after staying here for the nascar event. Free parking or airport transfer if needed. Check in/out was fast and easy with a warm genuine welcome from all staff. Everyone we met was friendly from the bell hop desk to check in staff and even other guests we spoke to (unlike other resorts on the strip). Rooms were big and clean and comfortable.   Food options were plentiful and varied from quick eat places to sit down steak house and food we had was top top quality (dont miss out on the hot dogs, great value gap filling snacks). Pool area was great with no shortage of comfortable sun loungers and music volume was just perfect. Not too noisy but loud enough to enjoy. Plenty of entertainment for everyone no matter what u want. We used to stay on the strip with the big brand hotels and venture out to independent hotels/casinos to escape the madness of the Strip. But from now on we will be basing ourselves at southpoint as its such a wonderful place. Big shout out to the girls serving drinks when we played slots, they were really friendly and fast with the drinks. We never had an empty drink glass in front of us. We attended the nascar races on both days and it was our first time at something like that and found it amazing. We got the free transfers to and from the hotel to the race track which ran like clockwork and very comfortable fast and easy. As we are not locals we wont get back to play for the points for the southpoint need for speed jackets next week so we are disappointed about that, but we did get a blanket each and got one of each of the bags on the promotion they are currently running. We are both gutted about not getting a jacket each as we know we would have earned enough points for 2 each. But that's the way it goes. Would love it if they could post us out one each...There is no downside to staying here. The place is just perfect for us and we can't wait to stay again.

reviews.title: Cheap Gamblen
reviews.text: A big casino hotel, much cheaper than the Strip. However, quite remote from the attractions, rooms are clean and large.  Buffet at the hotel is mega large and very cheap by Las Vegas standards

reviews.title: Nice hotel overall
reviews.text: Nice hotel. Good restaurants.The room had 2 beds and one was sloping. We paid extra for a view which was disappointing as the windows were dirty and we looked out on a roof. But the room was  nice and clean.

reviews.title: Very nice place
reviews.text: South Point is off the Strip, so it's calmer and less noisy.  We enjoyed a morning there.  They have a great variety of machines to play.

reviews.title: Great Garden Buffet at South Point Hotel Casino
reviews.text: We make a point of always visiting the breakfast or lunch Garden Buffet when we are in Las Vegas. I personally prefer the breakfast buffet. You get a discount if you use a Players card (available for free). There is a large variety of main food dishes, salads and desserts. The line moves very quickly as there is a large seating area. Parking is free.

reviews.title: Great Hotel
reviews.text: South Point is our favorite hotel to stay at when we are in Vegas.  Yes, it’s a bit south of “the action” but you can drive or take a taxi and be in “the action” within 15 minutes.  Our room was very spacious and extremely clean.  The bed was comfortable and the a/c worked great.  The bathroom was large and the shower provided instant hot water.  The doors are heavy and have a tendency to slam, even when we closed the door ourselves we still got a slamming noise.  The hallways can be very loud, especially on the weekends.  There is about an inch to inch and a half gap between the room door and the hallway which attributed to us being able to hear all the activity in the hallway.  Our last night (a Thursday) I put one of the bed pillows at the bottom of the door to shut out some of the noise.  All of the eating establishments are great, we never waited in line for the cafe for more than 3 minutes.  We love the “old school Vegas” feel of this hotel and are extremely grateful that this isn’t part of some corporate conglomeration.

reviews.title: Bad Customer Service by front  desk manager
reviews.text: I've been staying at South Point for years and have always enjoyed my visits until this past weekend, which completely changed my opinion of the hotel. Due to the appalling customer service I received from the front desk manager, John Ionnoti, I've decided I will never return.I was there to celebrate my birthday with friends and brought my fully documented service dog, as I have on previous trips. Upon arrival, I was shocked when Mr. Ionnoti claimed my dog was not an "approved service animal" and told me she could not stay. I calmly explained that she is a legitimate service dog and provided the appropriate documentation, but he refused to acknowledge it.His attitude was not only dismissive, but downright rude and condescending. I was left standing there, nearly in tears, with no place to go. When I asked if he could suggest a nearby hotel that accepts service animals, he coldly replied, "Google it," and told me that if I was seen with my dog on the property, security would escort me out.When I requested a refund, he responded with a degrading tone: "I'll give you back your $83," as if my experience and concerns were meaningless.I have never encountered such disrespect and lack of professionalism especially from someone in a management role. This experience completely ruined what should have been a special weekend. I'm still in disbelief that South Point allows someone so dismissive and unkind to represent their customer service team.This was not just poor service it was a complete disregard for basic decency and ADA protections. I hope South Point takes this seriously and addresses the behavior of this manager so that no other guest has to go through what I did.

reviews.title: We got robbed at this hotel
reviews.text: We got robbed by someone that had access to our room, we contacted the front desk and filed a police report. No one called us or contacted us the next day to tell us that they were sorry and they were handling the claim. We tried to get a copy of the paperwork that was submitted when we filed the police report and they refused to give us part of it. The manager did not care about anything that we had to say and was very rude.  Do not let anyone come and clean your room.

reviews.title: Nice rooms, not kid friendly.
reviews.text: We came with our family, including two children ages 7 and 3. Convenient for the event we were in town for. The rooms are a nice size and I appreciated the laminate floors. The employees were friendly and kind. However there was not one restaurant that had a children’s menu. It seems ridiculous to pay 20-30$ for meals that they eat 4 bites of.  And the pool is just ok. Not sure we will be back.

reviews.title: Early check in fee.....for what?
reviews.text: I have an issue with early check in fees. I can pay extra to check into my reserved room that is all set, or wait one hour till 2pm, and not pay the fee for the exact same room, while starting my stay with a bad taste in my mouth.

reviews.title: Le Garden Buffet of Las Vegas
reviews.text: The Garden Buffet is one of the best places to eat no matter what time you go Breakfast Lunch or Dinner it is by far the most reasonable price anywhere And don’t get me started on the Friday Night sea food buffet For the price you will get more than you can expect Over 25 times my wife and I have been there We have always left more than content If we could eat there on a weekly basis and could afford it Yes we Would Maybe it may not be to your expectations Well there are others but be prepared to pay double Enough Said

reviews.title: Meal saved by Dina!!
reviews.text: My wife and I dined at Southpoint Casino at the Coronado Cafe. We live here and bowl at Southpoint. A few weeks ago, we had to bowl a make up match in the evening. We decided to eat dinner early. My wife did not finish her dinner, but did not want to let the food go to waste. We asked the waiter if he could keep the food cold until later that evening. He said no! I saw a woman who looked like a manager. Her name was "Dina." I explained what we wanted. She said no worries, and we could keep our food in the fridge in the back until we returned. We returned after 9:30pm, and Dina brought our food back to us. What service! She was so nice and friendly. She is a credit to Southpoint!! Darold and Renee Cornell,Las Vegas

reviews.title: Avoid barbershop at all cost
reviews.text: Look, I have nothing bad to say about the hotel or resort.. just DO NOT get your haircut at the barbershop on site. They charge 100 for a shave and haircut. The shave was good but the haircut was possibly the worst haircut I've ever received especially at that price point. Had to get it re cut somewhere else that same day it was so bad. John was a super nice guy but it might be time he hangs up the clippers.

reviews.title: Perfect for Families!
reviews.text: Excellent Customer Service So many great people Pool was Fabulous! Bowling was crazy busy but fun once they got us inBartender at Pool was great especially with the Mock tails for kiddos Life Guards were helpful From Check In to Check Out the service and amenities were on par! Definitely be back and recommend to family and friends! Free Parking too!

reviews.title: Perfect place to stay safely
reviews.text: Great stay, free parking, not too expensive to stay safe, pretty sure rooms have had a make over, we have stayed here many times as don’t like being on strip, but still just a short drive up Blvd. Staff were very friendly, booked on line with Trivago, so was a little bit cheaper.Only downside side was Breakfast buffet was $73 as we didn’t have a members card, (but the new Denny’s across the road was perfect for $35). And there was a bit of a queue at times for elevators, but nothing spoilt our stay for the night before we flew home, car rental return just up the road on Gillespie and gas station on way to fill back up, all in all a perfect stay.

reviews.title: A real authentic casino!
reviews.text: After doing all the casinos in the strip I arrived at the South Point and I was not disappointed. Free parking, cinema, bowling, poker room... it's all there.The Garden Buffet is amazing and very reasonably priced. It is possible to play at gaming tables for $5. The place is perfect to escape tourists and crowds from downtown Vegas.

reviews.title: Not Bad, Not Great
reviews.text: The good: - quick and efficient check in, benefiting from an online checkin process if you choose to use that;- Del Mar deli is actually pretty good - not amazing - everything is served in styrofoam, including soup - would benefit from a sit down potential with real plates and bowls, but the soup and sandwich was till pretty decent - not New York deli decent, but not bad;- They have several restaurant choices, including a Steak and Shake, Japanese restaurant, steak house, Mexican, and Italian.- Nice sports book and horse racing betting lounge- 6 movie theaters on site along with bowling alley- nice pool areaThe less good:- room smelled of marijuana for 3/4 days… air conditioning made it worse it seemed, so, we shut it off and last day was not horrendous- a bit of a stretch to get to the strip, so you’ll be spending a few dollars on Uber’s- room, aside from the odor, was dated- elevators in the mornings were horrendous… 20 to 25 minutes to get to the lobby one morningNot the worst, not the best.

reviews.title: Don’t stay here.
reviews.text: Horrible!  Had to wait in line for elevator - half didn’t work.  TV in room broken.  Refrigerator broken -  needed it to keep meds chilled.  Made my reservation through 4/7.  On 4/6 I got a text to be out of my room by noon - check out time.Awful, awful!  Definitely do not recommend.

reviews.title: This was not what I expected when I booked a Junior Suite
reviews.text: We booked a Junior Suite for our recent stay. When we checked in the young woman at the desk told us it was on the 7th floor. Knowing that is a very low foot in Vegas I asked for something on a higher floor since we were paying for a suite. NOPE, can’t do it. We made our way to the 7th floor. As we exited the elevator we were greeted by a cloud of dust. Over half the rooms in our wing were in some state or disrepair due to a renovation. We arrived at our room, end of the hall, and the door was propped open by the latch. We knocked a few times went in, looked around, and called the front desk. They assured me it was our room. Part of the room looked newly renovated; the furniture looked like they went to a warehouse, took out a few things to place in the room, and called it a day. I then went to check out the view from our Junior Suite. We were overlooking the arena roof, had the parking lot on the right, a South Point tower on the left, and a gigantic billboard set front and center.  I went to the bathroom to freshen up before dinner. I called my husband in and asked him what was different about this room.It then occurred to us they had laced us in an ADA suite. We were running tight on time for our reservation at the Silverado steakhouse so we shrugged and went downstairs. Meal was very good as was the service. We decided to gamble for a big. 13000k+ points later (did not spend that much of my money but got to play on some of theirs) we went back to the room. Given the time, mowing it was for one night, we stayed.  We were there for an artist show. We were supposed to go back for one more night (we only live about 75 minutes away) but decided to stay at home and fight traffic rather than go through that again. This hotel is not worth the kind of money we paid for our room. I have had better comped rooms in Vegas than this one. BEWARE of where they send you.

reviews.title: March Madness!
reviews.text: You think you know Vegas. You think you’ve seen it all — the marble palaces, the chandelier-draped lobbies, the perfume of wealth wafting through hallways at the Wynn and Palazzo like some opulent cologne you’ll never quite afford. But then you check into South Point — and suddenly, everything you thought you knew gets flipped on its head, like a good steak in a hot pan.South Point doesn’t try to be hip. It doesn’t chase trends. There’s no mixologist here named Skyler muddling foraged herbs in a barrel-aged Negroni. What you do get is service — not just good service — generational service. The kind that remembers your name, your drink, and probably your kid’s birthday.During March Madness, South Point becomes a church — and Steve Stallworth and Bill Purcell are its high priests. These guys don’t just manage events, they orchestrate experiences. From the cavernous arena turned basketball sanctuary to the perfectly timed beer taps and betting windows, this isn’t amateur hour. It’s a masterclass in crowd control, hospitality, and knowing what makes sports fans tick.And let’s talk value. This is not “cheap.” This is smart. No $28 cocktails served with a wink and a side of regret. No half-assed buffets hiding under heat lamps. South Point is first-cabin service without the pretense. It’s the casino for people who remember when Vegas gave a damn. And thank the gambling gods — these guys still do.South Point, you sly devil. You’ve ruined me — in the best way.

reviews.title: fun is here.
reviews.text: I’m a local and I love this hotel, 11 restaurants, 16 movie theaters, 64 lane bowling alley and decent service.the south point arena is a big plus for me, bull riding and horse shows,the showroom always has something going on and don’t forget Kate’s korner ice cream and Del Mar deli. check out Steak ‘n Shake and my personal favorite don Vito’s.slot machines pay fairly well and the waitresses are pretty good, I tip when I win quite a bit of money. Sports book is a must, football games.check out this casino, very clean.

reviews.title: Why this hotel gets four out of five stars is Is not rooted in reality
reviews.text: I do not understand how this hotel could have 4 out of 5 stars. I recently brought my wife out on a business trip for a trade show with my company and we were all asked to save as much money as we could. Years ago We used to stay at the Luxor Hotel which back in 2002-2006 was a very good Choice for a hotel that would not break you especially if you could stay in the pyramid which we always chose. This time there was an overwhelming majority of reviews that said this hotel had gone way down in quality and had lots of pictures to show. Using TripAdvisor we found South Point Hotel and casino with almost 6,500 mostly positive reviews and figured that this must be a great hotel to stay at. We booked through my wife's work and in the confirmation showed that we had breakfast included in our room rate. When we were waiting outside of the airport to be picked up there was confusion among almost 20 passengers who were also waiting as to where we actually would be standing to be picked up by the shuttle bus Several people received different conflicting Locations as to where the shuttle bus would actually stop. I asked another shuttle bus driver who was stopped in the same area and he informed me that that shuttle would stop there. It did after a 15 minute delay from The programmed time. When we arrived at the hotel to check in we were told that no Breakfast was included in their room and that we would have to deal with my wife's company. Good luck on a Saturday afternoon. (I did receive a print out from my wife's work on Monday stating that breakfast was included but the hotel said they did not honor that). Starting on Saturday night through the following Thursday the 12 elevators for the building consistently kept breaking down. At any one time, there was only three to five elevators working for 24 floors for many hundreds of people trying to reach their rooms. At one point security had to be called to break up a major fight from people cutting in line and had to post security for the rest of the night because there were only two of the 12 Elevators working. When I asked several people over the course of our visit about the elevators they said that it was a common issue with that hotel.  I asked why would you keep coming back here and their simple explanation was they received free rooms for gambling.  Our room was okay however when my wife went to take a shower that first night, the water would not drain from the tub. Try 5 inches of swill water while you're trying to get clean.  I called the front desk and a service tech did come up within 15 minutes and dug out a large clump of hair from the drain.  It mostly worked after that.  Every day after 10:00 AM they were jackhammering the floor above us And above other rooms on our floor as they were renovating bathrooms all during the week. We ate in the buffet dining room for several meals and it was pretty good for the price. My wife did use the female salon and had her Hair and nails done and she was happy with the service. The one day I did not have to be at the trade show to open, I went down to the male salon to sit in the hot tub and was told it was broken. Overall the hotel was not a total disaster even though many nights we had to stand for at least 15 minutes to get up to our 8th floor. After being in Las Vegas almost a dozen times over the last 20 years for trade shows I have noticed and confirmed by taxi drivers that many of the hotels have Have fallen into disrepair after COVID wiped out most of the maintenance budgets of many of these hotels that were Affordable.  All you need to do is look at the price discrepancy between affordable hotels and the higher end hotels which are many hundreds of dollars a night more.  This was the only time our company had a booth at this trade show and my wife and I will not be back to Las Vegas.  Oh, One last point, between taxi And Uber rides to get to and from the Convention Center Because South Point is so far away $89.00/day, I would have spent almost the same as a $300 a night hotel. Therefore we did not save any money for the company as anticipated.

reviews.title: Stop before the Strip
reviews.text: We stopped here before heading to our hotel on the Strip.  It is a great local place.  It is big and wide open and very clean.  We had very good service at all the slots we played.  It was a fun time for the three of us for a few hours, and we will go back again.

reviews.title: Very disappointed
reviews.text: Smoking room an infection odor impregnated throughout the room and no possibility to ventilate Cleaning not done you have to ask Hotel very disappointing You have to love the crowd to go For those who love the casino there is what it takes I do not recommend

reviews.title: Go for the NFR
reviews.text: Respectful and friendly staff. Enjoy the all you can eat brunch when I go during the National Finals Rodeo. A lot to do in on spot especially for the equestrian community. Worth going if you choose to go to Vegas. I was able to get a coupon book for things around the Hotel and Casino that helped me save some money since I was staying there.

reviews.title: Document your check out!!!
reviews.text: Check out beware. I was there for collegiate bowling tournament my daughter was in with my 78 yo father with me. We left Sunday morning. While I’m sitting at airport they charge me $200. I called they said housekeeping report marijuana smoke smell in my room. I don’t even smoke period let alone marijuana. Unbelievable

reviews.title: Room dirty
reviews.text: So upon my arrival i go to my room and the first thing I see is a used condom on the bathroom floor behind the toilet. I reported it to management. Nothing got done, so make sure you inspect your rooms. I've been coming here for 4 straight years. Based on my overall experience, I won't be back. Management could have done something different other than roll their eyes at me and say sorry you want us to complete it unbelievable

reviews.title: Fun place for the NFR watch parties
reviews.text: Fun atmosphere!  loved the nightly watch parties for the NFR Easy  to navigate even when there were so many people attending events!. Clean, lots of food options. Clean restrooms!   Downside was just the parking garage and trying to leave events.

reviews.title: 10 Points for South Point!
reviews.text: We needed a last minute one night hotel in Las Vegas and South Point had a great deal.  The room had obviously been completely updated, the king bed was incredibly comfortable and all amenities were perfect for us.  We are locals in the winter and would never hesitate to stay at South Point again.  Our expectations were met and more!

reviews.title: Stayed here pre flight home; would do it again!
reviews.text: We rented a room for the day since we had a late night flight to go back home.  We'd come in from Death Valley and wanted a place to relax.  I'd recommend this for the proximity to the car rental return/airport.  They had a good happy hour at their restaurants and bars.  Lots of gambling areas, room was decent sized and comfortable.  Free valet parking was helpful too.  Staying here meant we could clean up, not worry about luggage, relax and get some gambling in before heading home!

reviews.title: Great trip, One complaint
reviews.text: Everything was great with one exception. Did the raiders shuttle and had alot of fun. We were told ahead of time that we got two drink coupons for each shuttle purchase. When we checked in they did not honor what we were told or what was advertised.. The check in employees said we only got two drink tickets for three reservations. There were six of us total. We were not happy with the false advertising, or the supervisors attitude. Two of us wrote to the Southpoint website, only to receive offensive response. We've decided that, if they don't get it figured out, we will try something else next time.

reviews.title: Good Night Sleep Before LAS Flight
reviews.text: My wife and I stayed here on our way back from Death Valley National Park. We were just in for one night to rest up for a morning flight out of LAS. We're not casino people. We just needed a nice bed and their hotel was the best deal in the vicinity of the airport.Check-in/out was an absolute breeze. They had a self check-in kiosk so we were able to get our room keys with no wait in line. We were also able to check out on our room TV, making both processes quick and easy.As for the room, it was spacious and the bed was super comfortable. We got a great night's sleep. The only issue we had was the bath spout didn't fully switch to the shower head when we pulled up on it, so it made for a little bit of a standing in a puddle while in the shower. A minor issue that didn't affect the quality of our stay. We would stay again.

reviews.title: A Transformative Las Vegas Experience: Embracing South Point Hotel and Casino After Decades of Loyalty to Caesars Palace
reviews.text: A Transformative Las Vegas Experience: Embracing South Point Hotel and Casino After Decades of Loyalty to Caesars Palace

reviews.title: Only 2 working elevators!
reviews.text: Only two elevators working for the higher floors. This is dangerous for many reasons. There is NO communication from the hotel staff regarding this. Plan ahead if you have a flight to catch as it could take you more than a half hour to get an over crowded elevator . This is a very busy weekend and week to come so wear your patience pants if you plan to stay here!

reviews.title: Stay away
reviews.text: We checked in for a week. The room next to us was under renovation. We called on our first day to check how long and they said it would last 8 hours but only for that day. The next day it started again. We called the front desk and the manager was the rudest person I’ve talked to in customer service. He told me it was a 24/7 casino and to deal with it, they wouldn’t move us rooms, offer a discount, or anything.

reviews.title: Nice Casino and buffet!
reviews.text: I have family that lives in the area and always bring us here when we visit from Florida. Not so much smoking, which I really appreciate. The buffet has always been very good every time we visit. Will we be back? Of cource we will. I'm sure you will enjoy your visit.

reviews.title: Another great stay
reviews.text: Our home away from home. Love the rooms, comfy beds. Cheap eats, midnight special of steak and eggs for $6.45. Lots of gaming options. Free comedy show Friday nights, dirty at 1230. Free airport shuttle. Movie theatre, bowling alley, pool, spa, bingo 5 times a day, this casino/ resort has it all! We have been to Vegas many times and don’t want to stay on the overpriced strip. Stay here. Oh yeah, free parking. We play table games and hardly have to pay for food with our comps. Will be back in April!

reviews.title: Cheap Bartender on staff after 10pm on Friday, October 4, 2024
reviews.text: South Point Hotel & Casino is a wonderful casino and the restaurant staff & food were great!  The only issue my family & I had was when my brother asked for a bottle of water (these are 8 oz. or less) - the bartender on staff stated that it would be $1. Yikes. After spending so much money at this casino and its restaurants, the guy couldn't give my brother 1 bottle. Wow . . . really stunk!

reviews.title: South Pointers for Life!
reviews.text: This is not our first stay at South Point; however, it was the best!  My husband and I visited Las Vegas for the Steelers/Raiders game.  The hotel offers game packages that include transportation by charter bus to the game.  We used it last year without any issues.  This time the wheelchair lift malfunctioned and we were not able to board.  The head valet assisting the bus driver informed the Front Desk Manager John about the situation.  They immediately began to look for a cab that allowed a power wheelchair to ride into it.  He had difficulties finding one.  My husband and I decided to sell our game tickets, but just as I was about to hit sell – John and 4 security officers appeared.  John offered us a solution to get to the game.  The security officers would load the wheelchair onto one of their trucks and they would use one of the cars for VIPs to take us to and pick us from the game.  It was his out of the box thinking that saved our vacation.John was awesome to work with and staff said the same.  We enjoy staying at South Point. The location is great.  There is not a lot of noise, the facility is always clean, the staff is friendly and knowledgeable.  And I assume it must be a good place to work because we see familiar staff faces each year.  Thank you again John, the valet staff and security officers for making this trip the best yet!

reviews.title: A Hidden Hotel Gem in Las Vegas!
reviews.text: We discovered the South Point Hotel & Spa a few years back and anytime we come to Las Vegas we stay here! This is located just south of the airport (a quick 10 ish minute ride from the airport) and has 11 restaurants, 2 bowling alleys, 16 movie theaters, a large equestrian center (they have rodeos here) a huge Bingo Hall (but this ain't your granny's Bingo - you can win big money here), lots of slot machines, plenty of table games and lots of parking (if you drive here or rent a car). They are very affordable, clean, and comfortable! Rooms are spacious with large bathrooms and the hotel staff is wonderful! Do yourself a favor and book massages at the spa... wonderful! See you guys in April for the Glass Expo!

reviews.title: South Point didn’t disappoint.
reviews.text: Great time at South Point.  Room was clean with a pool view.  We were able to check in early.  All the meals we had were awesome.  If we had a complaint it was the pillows.  We prefer a flatter pillow.  The 2 pool bartenders (Daniel and Bearto (sp?) were polite and provided great service!!

reviews.title: worth a stay
reviews.text: if you like us have visited las vegas  numerous times or you want somewhere quieter to stay than on the strip yet minutes away by car this is the place . Can,t fault it even though it was extra busy we found we could always get sun loungers at the pool ..  food was never a problem with loads of options to  try . whether table gambling or slots . this is a well run locals and tourist hotel well worth a stay here   .

reviews.title: Extraordinary
reviews.text: Pension in Vegas. Huge, but super comfortable.Nice pool, restaurant(s) very good. Bowling great, casino great.Well located about 15 minutes drive from the Strip.Large room, well equipped, however we had a view on a wall. No big deal for us, we had so many stars in our eyes. If I go back to Vegas, I go back to South Point.

reviews.title: Awesome
reviews.text: Starbucks located right inside the front door.  Full menu. I only got iced tea because it was so hot and it was the only thing that was going to quench my thirst. Pleasant staff and good quick service. Might be back tomorrow as it is right next door to my hotel

reviews.title: Absolutely First Class!!!
reviews.text: 100% impressed!!  Don’t know where to begin…Starting with checking in : we were welcomed like family .. no rush .. the hotel and amenities were explained in full with no confusion The room was absolutely spotless!!!No odd smells in hallways or room at all ..Beds were extremely comfortable with some of the best pillows on the planet !!The pool:: extremely clean pool and lounging area..the pool bar/deli was welcoming and ready to please  Casino :: some of the nicest dealers and casino management I have ever met / it was my fiancés first time playing roulette and the management was more than patient and accommodating Buffet and restaurants:::, Again, spotless!! Food was beyond the standard buffet fair and of course the servers were amazing !!Housekeeping deserves 10 stars !!To sum up our experience :: I will always stay at South Point ! I have never been treated so well in Las Vegas.. please give this hotel your business.. I promise you will not be disappointed!!

reviews.title: A visit worth taking
reviews.text: This is our favorite hotel for the last 10 years or so we have been coming to South Point. We were not even checked in when my brother won a jackpot on the Evel Knievel machine. Everyone here is very nice including Michelle in Host services she helped us when we checked out. Sarah is awesome in bingo. Ana and Robert in Coronado Cafe are excellent. Sarah Ochoa and Gabby in the business office we're very nice and helpful in wrapping some of our items to pack to come home. Roulette dealer Therna  was very accommodating in spinning the numbers that I had been betting on. We especially wish to thank Kelly in the cashiers box, we've seen her and said hello every time we've been for the last 4 to 5 years. It's always our pleasure to visit with her for an extra minute or two. She's very nice to deal with. We thank everyone that we dealt with during our two stays at the South Point.

reviews.title: IM IN VEGAS 6 months a year! THAT IS MY FAVORITE PLACE
reviews.text: From the moment we arrived, we were greeted by the warmest and friendliest host, making check-in a breeze. Our room was ready well before 3 p.m., setting the tone for an unforgettable stay. We were there for the photo booth convention, and I instantly fell in love with the hotel. The rooms were impeccably clean, and the service was both swift and welcoming. Everywhere you go, the bartenders are there to brighten your day with their friendly demeanor. And of course, I have to mention the oyster bar—my absolute favorite! Their happy hour is unbeatable, with talented chefs who spoil you with delightful little samples. Since February, I’ve returned four times, and I know it won’t be the last. Can’t wait to go back!

reviews.title: Hidden gem off strip
reviews.text: Fun clean place that in all reality you dont have to leave. Many food and entertainment choices. Clean and modern feel. Front desk was awesome to deal with and very informative.  Parking garage on ground and easy to navigate.  Only drawback, the casino is very smokey and smells of it.  Not terrible but detectable. Unlike many Las Vegas Casinos.

reviews.title: Great stay - we would love to come back!
reviews.text: - large room- beautiful view of pool landscape and mountains (22. Stock)- nice, uncrowded casino - Bowling alley and small arcade available - to the delight of our son- Restaurant selection ok (but we were mostly eating outside the hotel) - Parking garage and parking for free! - The pool is nice and big and the whirlpool is great - Coupon booklet (which we didn't use - somehow there was nothing for us) - For us the location was great - for the activities we parked at Luxor, Sphere, Fashion Mall and Freemant StreetWhat we didn't like so much: - no refillable care products - a shame - the garden buffet is good, but from 9 years old the full price should be paid - that was too much for us (a child can't eat that much at all) - here a coupon would have been nice especially for children that they can at least eat for free or for a small price at the buffet (so we were outside the hotel for dinner) - at breakfast we ate a few times anyway at the buffet

reviews.title: No Grace, Rude Management
reviews.text: Rude and Arrogant management. Our reservation had us on the 20th from the 1st email. Somehow in the matrix it was altered to the day before. At checking the reservationist did not give us a receipt. In the confusion we asked to pay for the extra day and the management wanted to charge us 2 times our initial price. We hadn’t learned about the error until we were getting kicked out. Never will go back. DO NOT RECOMMEND. Casino/Hotels make a ton of money. A small price adjustment would have been a small price that would made a world of difference compared to what was Offered in wanting to Charge 2 times more, (then on their site it was $20 less). If Pissing people off is more important. Well done!

reviews.title: Best Hotel/Casino in Las Vegas
reviews.text: South Point is quite simply, the best place to stay, play and eat in Las Vegas.   The hotel is old school and has lots of loss leader food and drink specials.  My favorites are the buffet which serves quality prime rib, the hotdog cart which has the best hotdogs I have ever eaten for $1.50 each and the Coronado Cafe which features a fantastic $19.95 complete Porterhouse steak dinner available 24 hours.   The hotel and common areas are all extremely clean and they work very hard to keep it that way.  Beds are very comfortable and rooms are quiet.The casino is always extremely busy because of great odds on video poker and table games.  The video poker inventory is without equal in the state of Nevada and South Point boasts hundreds of games paying back well over 99%.  This was my third visit to the property and it has become my "home" casino.  It is privately owned and does not have to please shareholders, only the customers so it can offer great deals as loss leaders.Employees are all very friendly and genuinely go out of their way to help.  Bar service is the best I've ever had in Las Vegas.  This property is a far cry from the corporate-owned megaresorts on the Strip where they think they're doing you a favor by letting you in the door.  Ripoff food, hotel and gambling so common on the Strip does not exist at South Point.

reviews.title: Not going back and not recommending
reviews.text: Tri State uses this venue every year for their seminar.  I have not been here in 5 years and I won't be coming back.  They close the pool and hot tub area at 8 pm.  They didn't close it so early in the past.  Not only do they close early in this hot summer, but at 7:55 the lifeguards are running everyone out.  I won't come back just for this reason.  I'll go somewhere else where the pool and hot tub stay open much later.

reviews.title: Atmosphere, amenities, restaurants awesome.  Slot machines, terrible.
reviews.text: I would rate the variety of food and fun, and atmosphere of the overall resort, a 5 out of 5.  It's a very lively place to be, with something to do for everyone.  A 24-hour Starbucks with an ice cream parlor right next to it is a very nice touch.This review, however, is from a locals perspective on slot machine gaming compared to the rest of the Vegas casinos.  And with that, I can tell you that South Point has some of the tightest slot machines in the entire Las Vegas valley.  Go for the amenities, play the tables, enjoy the restaurants, cafe and buffet, but don't expect to see much in the way of winning if you are there to play the slot machines.I've seen old reviews, posted by South Point, on how they supposedly decided to run with looser slots, and that is absolutely not true.  My wife and I have played approx. $50-$60k per year ($1-$4 bets on all types of slots) across all the casinos in Vegas, for the past 15 years.  Southpoint is one of the few casinos where you can play a few grand, betting only a few bucks a spin, and not have ANY action whatsoever for the entire session.  You end up having a very short night, which is a terrible experience.   It's happened so many times over the years that we've decided 2024 is now the year to cut South Point out of our list of places to play.  We only stop by South Point to run in to grab a Starbucks late night before a long drive.

reviews.title: Family stay for USBC Open, disgusted by filthy room floors and lack of housekeeping services for 3 night stay.
reviews.text: Family stay for USBC Open, disgusted by filthy room floors and lack of housekeeping services for 3 night stay.

reviews.title: Great hotel
reviews.text: Always a good experience at south point!  It is annoying how they Market Price the rates so it goes from 89/night to 300/ night in a flash.. I have been booking other places as they get pricier and pricier.  Shame as it was my go to place for years.  A lot of the older vegas hotels are upping their game so if you don’t have a horse or want to bowl you can get better value on the weekends elsewhere..

reviews.title: Totally Great Experience!!
reviews.text: My wife and I stayed at the South Point for the first time for a quick trip to Vegas. So glad we did! The atmosphere, food, room, and staff were great. Plus, the slot machines were very hot!! We usually stay on the Strip but we will be returning to South Point in the fall.

reviews.title: Good place to stay!
reviews.text: Great hotel with a clean room and awesome restaurants. Also, a plus that there is a Starbucks right inside the hotel. A downside is that it's just far enough away from the strip to be a little trip getting to and from. The bowling ally and movie theater are also nice to take a break from gambling.

reviews.title: Always A Good Experience
reviews.text: Always a good stay - have to know when to eat at different places at the hotel to avoid long lines but that is to be expected.  Jewel and Wangy who write reviews in June and July of this year seem like whiners - have stayed many times at South Point and not experienced ANY of the alleged stuff they claimed happened so their reviews should probably be thrown out along with really anyone complaining about this hotel and casino.  Speaking of casino, whining about not paying out just means you don't know which machines and what time to play them.  Payout is pretty average in Las Vegas for slot machines so people complaining about that should just find somewhere else to stay and somewhere else to gamble.  I'll be there again next month I think anyway so looking forward to it.

reviews.title: What a gem!
reviews.text: First time staying at South Point and no regrets!  If you want the Vegas experience with scantily clad women and drunks walking up and down the Strip, then this is not the place for you. We have stayed in many of the strip hotels over the years, so this was a refreshing change.  Check-in was easy and fast - only took about 10 minutes at 4:00pm on a Monday.  Had a king non-smoking room on the 22nd floor with a view of the pool and stayed 4 nights.  Beds were comfortable. We had a fridge and a coffee maker with free coffee pods!  That is unusual in Vegas.  Bathroom was nice with a separate area for tub and toilet. There was a lighted make-up mirror on the wall.  Shampoo, conditioner, lotions and soaps were good and plentiful.  Housekeeping was prompt each day.  It was 116 that week, so we were happy that our room stayed cool. There is a safe in the closet and plenty of USB ports/plugins on each side of the bed.  The room as a little dark, but if you turned on all the lights, it was fine.  We didn't hear any noises at night and did not smell smoke on our floor.We had no issues with the elevators, but there were times we saw people standing in line waiting for one - mostly in the evenings.  It was very easy to get from the rooms to the pool area and fitness center.The 24 hour fitness center was great - looks out on the pool area and has all the machines and equipment you could want, plus towels and sanitizers to keep things clean.  Treadmills had a blue tooth connection for airpods.The pool area was nice even in the excessive heat - there was shade in the first part of the day and again around 4:00pm.  It was nice that it stayed open until 8.  We used the hot tub also -it is in a shaded area and had jets that were forceful!  Towels were easy to get and loungers were easy to find and move into shade if needed.  They have a gazebo area that is shaded with tables and chairs.We did have a rental car and the parking garage was free and they were actually cleaning the floors one of the days! It is an easy walk to the casino from the garage - a little farther to the room elevators.  They have a free shuttle from the airport (unheard of in Vegas!) so you could go without a car if you were not going anywhere else.  It's pretty far south of the Strip - probably 15 minutes.We ate breakfast and lunch at the Garden Buffet several times - food was better than we had last March.  We used our loyalty cards and points to get some $$ off, which made it very affordable. Great omelets made to order, great French Toast and plenty of other variety. The snack bar in the Bowling Center was a pleasant surprise - sandwiches and salads for very reasonable prices.  We ate at the Steak and Shake late one night, and it was good too.  Coronado Cafe has great late-night specials from midnight to 6:00am, but be prepared to stand in line.We also did the Senior movie for $4 at the cinema - nice experience!This hotel is well managed - overall it was a great experience. The crowd is mostly bowlers, locals or rodeo people.  Not the glitz and glamour of the strip, but a clean, nice, respectable crowd.  Felt very safe here and we will stay here again!

reviews.title: Superb Adult Vacation
reviews.text: This was the best adult vacation destination I have ever been to.  Every member of the staff was wonderful.  We were treated as valued guests and enjoyed the property immensely.  The only complaints we had were the bath towels are too small and the pool closed TOO EARLY (8 pm)!The Rigatoni with Italian Sausage at Don Vito’s was the VERY BEST pasta dish I have ever eaten!!!!!We only ate off the property one time because the food variety and quality was excellent!!!  The breakfast and lunch buffets have something for everyone and the Coronado Cafe has superb Prime Rib!  Also, try their Rodeo Wrap with fries-you won’t be disappointed!!!!!  Even the hot dog and BBQ at the bowling alley snack bar were excellent!  We just can’t say enough about it all!!!!!!I can’t wait to return to Vegas and South Point!!!!

reviews.title: Smelly and Dishonest Customer Service
reviews.text: Where do I start? Hmmm. Check-In. We advised hotel months in advance we had a late flight. They confirmed our room would be available. We paid for a "Premium View" room. Well, if you call that looking at the side of condo towers next door and the pool. No strip or mountain view rooms available at check-in! Wow! We still paid full price! They said we could switch rooms two days later. Hard to do with kids and stuff already unpacked. And they allowed :30 to do it. We missed all the fireworks with our view. Not the plan after spending $3k to get to Vegas.Customer Service does not care a bit about anyone!Next up. Non Smoking floor? Well, the hallways smell like ciggy smoke. Weird? Smells? If you like smells, this is the place for you. Casino floor smells like urinal cakes. No doors on bathroom entries by restaurants. That is really bad! Pool area smells like a horse barn from the horse arena next door. Two times there were piss puddles in the elevators. Plenty of drunks here for the price point. Lots of dirty people from south of the border. May explain the pee?Parking ramps always full. Arcade for kids, yes. But each game costs 2.25 to 3.50! Not kidding! Your kids will lose more money than you will gambling! FACT! We did!Lots of bowling going on. Never a lane open for family fun. Always full of pros. So you wont be bowling here either!In all, not a place to take a family! Not affordable! Poor customer service! Did I mention the slot machines dont payout? That too! Only good thing was the food at the mexican restaurant! 10/10!

reviews.title: Good place
reviews.text: We like stopping at the South Point casino and playing there.  It has a calm, fun atmosphere.  The sports book is very good.  They have a huge variety of slots and table games.  The casino floor is spacious and open.  It is not as wild and crazy as the Vegas Strip.

reviews.title: Staff hospitality, staff training, and biased management towards staff
reviews.text: Experience at the garden buffet was terrible. They insinuated that we didn’t pay and hospitality of the staff was very unwelcoming. The way that your staff acts shows the atmosphere of the hotel as a whole. The training of all the staff overall (pool, food staff, hotel front desk, etc) was a bit off. They should be retrained.  During our experience at the garden buffet the staff didn’t let our kids go eat. We paid for them and they said that they weren’t allowed to let us in due to us “ not paying". We showed them the receipt that we paid for everyone but they said the manager had to come confirm us in. The other people around us were allowed in no question asked. When explaining  to the women who lets the guests in I said " my kids are hungry we paid can you please let them in?" she replied with "no I cannot".  When the manager confirmed, they let us in and we just let the situation go. Another incident took place at the pool where a family was accused of dropping feces in the pool when the family who did drop it left as soon as it happened. The pool staff called security on them and was very aggressive. Never going to this hotel again do not recommend!

reviews.title: Home away from home
reviews.text: My favorite hotel in Las Vegas. It is clean and comfortable, and most of the employees are happy, helpful and professional.  Michael Gaughan has created a home away from home.Host Jamie Lewis , Bartender Craig Bauer and Steakhouse Server Lito are just a few examples of the creme de la creme that Mr Gaughan has secured to represent his establishment.

reviews.title: Thank You South Point
reviews.text: Hotel was great,food reasonably priced and good. Has that Vegas feel without the chaos of the strip. We rent a car everytime so not a big deal the distance to the strip. Security is also top notch. We left a voucher in a machine late at night after a few cocktails and I walked to cash it in at a redemption close by,realizing I did not have ticket and went directly back to the machine I was playing and somone cashed it out! Could not have been more then 15 seconds. So ,I found security and they were on it.  All this within about 4 minutes total. Luckily I was using my player card,they tracked the ticket number down by number and canceled it in their system before the person cashed it in. They hand paid me the amount of voucher! THANK YOU SOUTHPOINT SECURITY TEAM! It was our first time staying there and will not stay anywhere else from now on. Staff is excellent.

reviews.title: Great place for gaming and to relax away from strip
reviews.text: First time here and will be back. As a former local this is the kind a place I would visit. The crowd here is a mix of locals and older people. This is not a LV strip experience but rather a Vegas experience.Check in was easy and staff were great.Room is where I had some issues. First of all, while it was clean and spacious, there was a noticeable smell of cleaning products which eventually faded. Second issue was that the curtain did not close all the way so light started coming in as soon as the sun came up. Lastly, not sure if it was because we were on a lower floor (4th to be exact) but it was noisy and got a lot of noise, mostly from what sounded like a leaf blower. Other than that it was fine. Nice touch was that there were a couple pair of Southpoint slippers (not top dollar but appreciated) waiting for us. Not sure if it was because it was our first time or they do that for everyone.Bowling alley was fun and reasonable I think. Paid $63 for 4 people and 3 games. Included shoe rental. They have food there however we did not try any.They have plenty of dining options and we choose Steak and Shake. Was not that good over priced and would not go there again.Gaming. Loved playing here. This is was Vegas used to be. 3:2 black jack with $10 minimums. Hand shuffle and not like 8 decks. Sat at a table and was able to play for some time. Went up and down bet from 10 to 50 but I was able to stay on the table and enjoy myself unlike on the strip. Other table games had the lower minimums as well.And staff was great. Asked for extra pillow and they were brought right up. Left clothing in the room and they kept it and was able to get it back from lost and found 2 days later.

reviews.title: Short trip but nice
reviews.text: I arrived Tuesday around 10pm the staff got me checked in quick, the room was clean and affordable. The poker room was good action but low key. Abigale at the desk is on point as were others, the burger in the bowling alley was 10.99 and very good, and the midnight specials are super cheap. I will stay there again next time.

reviews.title: Fun place to stay
reviews.text: Southpointe is a nice place to stay if you don’t want the craziness of the middle of the strip. Fabulous amenities..many slots and poker tables. Outstanding restaurants and all of the staff are so very nice. Our room was large and comfortable. The only thing I found objectionable..and it is a personal opinion..is the outfits the cocktail waitresses have to wear are ugly..sleazy..and exploitative. Time to stop catering to men ogling and get them something pretty to wear. Wearing something classy is way more appealing and tasteful.

reviews.title: Get Your Eat On!
reviews.text: Joined family at the Garden Buffet for lunch!  Food was filling and a great variety to choose from.  Great atmosphere and service. Reasonable prices 7/$126.  We weren't guest of the casino/hotel, but we did play slots and enjoyed their buffet.

reviews.title: Memorial day 2024 Family Getaway
reviews.text: As I am writing this, Ive just arrived home from Las Vegas and I had to immediately post a review of this hotel. First off, I came with my family for my 40th birthday celebration weekend, and from the start, I was a very good one. Upon coming in from the parking structure and into the casino, I noticed that the casino was very big, however , everything was within reach from starbucks to all the eateries. Second, checking in was a breeze and I have to say, very very secure by scanning your ID. The front desk lady, who I cannot remember her name, was very kind to move us from the 17th floor down to the 5th, thus taking away my families fear of tall buildings. She was very pleasant and extremely helpful. Customer service for the entire 2 night stay was 5/5 stars all the way. When it comes to food, we did try the Coronado cafe. The food was pretty good, however if there was ever any complaint about this hotel, is that the beef barley soup had zero flavor to it, and my chicken in the cesar salad was very cold. With that said, we did eat at Zenshin that evening for dinner, and to be honest, the food served there had some of the best ramen Ive ever had in my life. I am half Japanese, though not a ramen snob, but for a place like this to serve noodles in this fashion? That was pretty amazing. I also ordered the salmon skin salad, along with a freshly fried soft shell crab tempura style, and I was blown away. The room was gorgeous. The hardwood floors made it feel very homely, and the bed and beddings smelled fresh and very nice. Bathroom wise, nothing to complain about at all. The tub , toilet and sink areas were all extremely clean, and very nicely polished. All in all, I would and will definitely stay here again. When  we got there , there must have been some type of bowling tournament happening, and it was neat to see all the folks get ready to do their thing. Keep up the amazing work South Point.

reviews.title: Top stay in Las Vegas
reviews.text: Beautiful Hotel with Casino, Swimming Pool, Spa, Bowling, Cinema, and several restaurants at the gates of Las Vegas. Large and free parking, large and comfortable rooms, the only flaw is the 70s bathtub, but otherwise really excellent! Very organized for baggage delivery and parking, quick check in despite the queue. Highly recommended!

reviews.title: Best Ever!!  No more strip hassle!
reviews.text: Well, this was our first visit to an outside the center strip area in 50 Years. We had a nice room overlooking the pool on the 15th floor.Housekeeping was great. Keurig in each room was a surprise. AC worked great and room had a refridge. Only downer was the bed was not the best and pillows the worst. South Point was self contained. Great casino with low bets. Restaurants were many options. There were deals to be had at all of them. Bowling center, Equestrian arena, sports book, and a GREAT pool area "could use more shade". We will NEVER go to a strip hotel again. South Point is ours now. Thank You to all.Jerry The K

reviews.title: Beautifully remodeled!
reviews.text: Beautiful room, nice amenities. Friendly staff. Stayed overnight to visit friends. Did not visit the casino other than to walk through. Ate dinner with friends, so didn’t get to dine at lodge, nor use pool or spa. Would stay again, and for more than one night.

reviews.title: Housekeeping issues
reviews.text: Pay a lot of money wFor a room. Asked at registration if we wanted housekeeping. I said yes No housekeeping was done. Had to call for towels etc and then waited quite some time for them to arrive.  Other than that,  this resort is great. So much to do.

reviews.title: South Point is Our Vegas Home
reviews.text: Just returned from a Monday-Friday (April 29-May 3) stay at South Point. This is the first time we've stayed there rather than the Grandview condos across the street.  We've never seen the place so busy except maybe for the first rounds of March Madness. It was nuts. All casino hotels in Vegas should study South Point to see how they do it. There was a huge bowling tournament, a Towing Industry convention, and a five-day radio controlled car competition.  By Friday the Derby crowd was showing up. The Race Book was full to overflowing, and there's a ballroom viewing party today (Saturday).  The casino was busy every day, morning, noon and night. Drink service on the floor was good once a server found us, but it sometimes took awhile to get an order because it was so busy.  We had pretty good luck this trip, though of course that's not always the case.South Point has been our gambling/entertainment hub for several years.  We really appreciate the stability of the employees, many of whom have been there since it opened.  They say they are well treated and are generally happy and helpful.   Our room was on the 24th floor and was great.  It had a very comfortable king bed, two upholstered chairs, a small table with two chairs, and a desk with chair.  Maid service was daily with fresh towels and bedding if you choose.  Toiletries were above average quality and there were even two sets of slippers, nice enough to bring home. Though the hotel was full, we didn't hear our neighbors. Just the usual slamming doors and occasional talking of people in the hallway. Wednesday two or three elevators (there are six) were out of order and lines got quite long at times. Other days it wasn't an issue. Our room looked west over the pool. We only visited the pool once.  Nice pool, separate kiddy pool, and large hot tub.  It opens at 10 am but after 11 there's very little shade. It closes at 6 pm, which seems too early.We ate at Don Vito's, Primarily Prime Rib, the Coronado Cafe, and had the breakfast and lunch buffets. Prices continue to creep up (inevitable with food inflation being so bad) but the food is both tasty and high quality in the restaurants and the buffet. It's all still a very good value. Yesterday was Seafood Buffet night. It opened at 3 pm. We had to leave for the airport at 3:30, but people were lining up for the buffet at 1:30. They even brought their own folding stools! We talked to a few waiting in line. Mostly locals for whom it's a weekly, monthly, or whatever event. They consider it a real bargain.South Point provides a free shuttle to and from the airport. We used it coming and going. The schedule is available on their website.  Few Vegas hotels offer one.  It's a money saver, since without it cab or Uber fare to/from South Point can range from $20 to $40.  It would be nice if there were better public transportation options from South Point.  A bus comes right to the casino, but getting to the strip using it requires a transfer and a fair amount of time.  Ubers and Lyfts are generally hanging out in the parking lot, quick to arrive if wanted.  The "bottom line" is that SP continues to be our first (and only) choice, whether staying there or at the Grandview. We didn't leave the property for our entire stay. I sure hope they keep it up. The success of their formula is evident in the crowds. My only complaint (and I mean this as a compliment to them) is that the place has maybe become too popular!

reviews.title: Family comes 1st
reviews.text: When in Vegas Southpoint is my one stop playground.  I’m 72 and my children live in Vegas…we all love the convenience, hospitality, bowling center, theater, and Coronado Cafe. I wish I cold win in the casino once in awhile but that’s not on you SP

reviews.title: A pretty good overall experience; would return.
reviews.text: This place is obviously off the strip and has little of the "glamor" of those mega-properties. But that has advantages: It's not small but "smaller" so you don't have to walk two miles to an event or to your room.  The elevator service is good (an amenity not to be overlooked in the mega-hotels). The rooms are nice and large at about 500 sq ft. The furnishings are modest, not new or high-fashion, but fine really. The bathroom could use a bit more light but has a water-closet area for the toilet and shower, so two people could use it if need be.  The casino is fine (not a huge gambler) and they have what you'd want.  Friends liked that there were lower limit tables if that's what you prefer.  The sports book is pleasant. Several bars. Valet service quicker than most places, which is big!   Unlike many Vegas hotels, this had ample front-desk help for check-in.   Very good price-point, even over SuperBowl long weekend. And this location avoids the annoying strip-area traffic, while still being fairly close to the stadium, golf course(s), whatever.  I would definitely return.

reviews.title: My stay at South Point Casino
reviews.text: I enjoyed the restaurants for quality and variety.  Liked the fact that both Coronado Cafe and the gift shop were open 24/7 for convenience, versus other hotels.  Casino provided comfortable environment and l loved all the video poker machines.

reviews.title: Great hotel
reviews.text: Great hotel, got everything you need, 2 small problems, the wi/fi is not good and is you win over 1200 bucks they do not offer any taxation help which as I am from UK would have been good. The bar staff are all brilliant and the buffet is excellent (big shout out to David at the egg station, really nice chap.) In modern Vegas it is probably the only place I would stay, proper old school.

reviews.title: Wonderful!
reviews.text: We have stayed here several times, and we always enjoy it because it is not on the strip, so the hotel is newer, and the pool area is not as crowded. The casino, restaurants and rooms are always clean. The spa and restaurant staff are wonderful. Plenty to do right inside the hotel like movie, bowling, gambling, and watching sports. Plenty of free parking and it's easy to order an Uber to go downtown. We have never had any problems here whatsoever and I really recommend trying this hotel/spa.

reviews.title: Good times at South Point Hotel
reviews.text: A group of us stayed at South Point to watch the football playoffs and to have some good times. We could not have stayed at a better hotel, from the excellent cuisine to the clean and comfortable rooms, you can’t go wrong!

reviews.title: Great weekend
reviews.text: This hotel and casino is top notch. The rooms are big and clean with no carpeting which is great. The casino although they allow smoking was relatively free of smoke. All employees I talked with were very friendly. My only complaint was with the elevators I literally waited 15 minutes to go down to the casino at 810am on saturday because it seemed like only 3 elevators worked out of 6. With all the hotels we have stayed at this was the best. I would definitely stay here again .The resort fees were cheaper the all others plus free parking.

reviews.title: My favorite buffet in Vegas
reviews.text: South Point only proves covid did not kill buffets, greed did. When I am in Vegas which is alot I eat breakfast there everyday or brunch on the weekends, the staff is exceptional, have become friends with Dave who makes omelettes as well as most of the staff there, great people. But i really like the food and price as well, I get an omelette then top it with mushrooms from one of the stations, then off to the fruit for a full plate of the variety they have there, then their bakery for the deserts has to be one of the best in the entire city, I get banana cream, coconut cream, or chocolate cream myself but they have alot to pick from. And as good as that is, I like everything about the South Point from gambling to bowling, it is it's own little city in one location. Just hope they do not change everything good about the place like a few others I could name have done in the name of greed. Which is why I go here now instead of some bigger strip places that I used to go to more. Keep up the great work South Point. Thx.

reviews.title: South Point has a lot to offer
reviews.text: I really impressed with all the activities that South Point Casino had to offer for all guests.  I personally really enjoy having breakfast at their Garden buffet.  Still very good and Still priced reasonably...This place has something to offer for most people....

reviews.title: If 0 stars were allowed
reviews.text: ( this should be a half star or no star) On Friday January 19th 2024 I was playing high limit video poker and was approached by a slot attendant named Lyn she started talking to me while playing 75 dollars a hand. She stood over me  and continued to talk, I did not reply after ignoring her I just "shoed" her away.  I asked for a supervisor and asked him to tell her to please stop bothering me while i am gambling. On Saturday morning I spoke to the slot dept manager Mr. James Brown. He assured me that he would address this issue.Well I go saturday night the 20th for dinner with my wife. I go back to high limit and play hit a small jackpot and I go elsewhere in the casino. After 45 minutes I hit another jackpot. Waiting to get paid the shift manager Shelly , Lyn and Casey all from the slot dept came over with a security guard  to pay my winnings and I was told by Shelly I am no longer allowed to play in the slots at the  Southpoint I guess my money is no good in slots at the Southpoint Casino..

reviews.title: It's hard not to like South Point
reviews.text: What you see is what you get at South Point, and it's hard not to like their good value, non-pretentious vibe, and fair offerings.  They have a large facility, plenty of free parking, loads of good value food outlets, an excellent sports book, poker area and slot machine selection, and the rooms are always fairly priced.  That's probably why the place is always crowded.  And as a business, they earn that repeat custom fair and square.  While it's a place largely focussed on locals, I also find that they do a very reasonable job of looking after regular visitors to Vegas like myself.  When I recently stayed a few nights at Mandalay Bay at the start of a 12 night trip where I stayed across several properties, I didn't even bother to gamble a penny at MB, and just did all my gambling during that part of my trip at South Point.  That will blow my future comps at Mandalay/MGM for a while, but that's ok, I'll just stay at South Point instead.😉.  I like it here, and I'll definitely be back.  Back for the good value, the real atmosphere, and the fair deal they offer.

reviews.title: Great Option Off The Strip
reviews.text: We needed a comfortable place to spend 2 nights prior to an international flight. We are non-gamblers. This hotel was just right. Situated south of the strip, the hotel offers spacious, quiet, comfortable rooms and beds. The self-parking is ample, with valet-parking available as well. There are 6 in-house eateries, ranging from all-you-eat buffet style to more fashionable restaurants. Checking-in/out was a breeze. We will definitely be back!

reviews.title: First time staying: we will be back!
reviews.text: Quick overnight on a Thursday. It was our first time staying there, and we very much enjoyed it. Our room was a Premium View King, and it was lovely. We liked the layout, appreciated the fridge, and liked the express elevator for floors 14 and up (we were on 17). The bathroom was roomy and bright, the bed was comfortable and the pillows were just right! We explored the hotel amenities (bowling alley, equestrian area) without partaking, and they were hopping! Gambled a bit on the slots, enjoyed solid drink service, and then called it a night around 11:30. Enjoyed the buffet the next morning

reviews.title: 10 STARS, The best place to stay. Very clean and exceptionally nice rooms.
reviews.text: Exceptionally clean and gorgeous hotel and Casino. Rooms are very large and very nice. Super nice furniture and bed is amazingly comfortable. Casino is huge and so many nice places to eat inside. High quality furnishings and nice bathrooms.

reviews.title: Good value, clean and comfy
reviews.text: Our first time back in years as we stayed a few times when the hotel first opened, then moved to the strip for subsequent trips. Decided to try South Pointe again as the strip has become more expensive, parking a hassle etc. We were very pleased. The premium king was a good size room, wood floors, free slippers. Clean. Bed comfortable. Parking free. Only complaint is bathroom drains very slow, especially the shower, also old shower head with no adjustment. Plenty of hot water though. Food is mediocre but lots of choices. Overall a good value.

reviews.title: The best casino off strip and my favorite in vegas in general
reviews.text: South point is a great casino, been there multiple times since 2015.  It has pretty decent rooms, pretty much vegas standard at the very least.  Southpoint has great lighting, a really really good buffet which is important after covid and they have other great restaurants inside as well as one of the only few steak &shakes around.   They also have rodeo events sometimes and they hold nascar when its around.    The casino area is really nice, has lose slots, love the coloring and there's a lot of great staff.  They also have some of the best cocktail waitress uniforms and babes around if that's your thing, here's hoping they never change their uni's.  They pretty much have it all, and its the best off strip casino bar none.

reviews.title: Humid Rooms, no fans in bathroom
reviews.text: This is my second time in one month staying at South Point. I live about an hour away, but like to stay in Vegas when my work schedule is busy and I am too tired to drive home. I have stayed on the 6th floor and the 4th floor. Both times the room is sort of humid and has no airflow. Yes, there is AC, but no circulation. The bathroom and sink area, although separate, do not have fans to help with moisture. I called down to the front desk and asked for a fan, of any kind, and they said they don't have any. Guess I will have to pack a small desktop fan for my next stay.Other than that, the bed is comfortable, it's relatively quiet, the parking is free, and there's a Starbucks in the lobby.

reviews.title: Good value stay
reviews.text: We stayed for four days following the labour day weekend. There is ample free parking and it is well connected to get around whether that's to the strip or out to some of the national parks. The rooms are large and well appointed if a little dimly lit. The beds were super comfortable and there was a good sized fridge in the room. The cleanliness could be improved as there was a lot of dust in the room but nothing terrible. The pool is nice though has no umbrellas so you need to bag the chairs that happen to be in the shade. There are lots of restaurants of different £-£££ depending on what you're looking for. All in all we had a really nice stay there and would stay again.

reviews.title: perfect
reviews.text: free parking and lots of it. reasonable price and clean great room.  buffet is reasonably priced as well.  close to the strip and everywhere else.  its my go to hotel when in vegas.  except when i have to be close to the lake.  then i stay at the campsite

reviews.title: I'll keep returning
reviews.text: This was not my first stay here and it definitely won't be my last. From the Valet to housekeeping everything is top notch.  Breakfast Buffet on the weekend was delicious. No waiting and plenty of food at the stations. The pool was spectacular. The pool bar service exceeded expectations. Gaming wasn't good to me but it won't prevent me from returning.  Great job!

reviews.title: A casino with horses!
reviews.text: I can't believe theres a casino with horses, if I knew this we would be staying here instead of our hotel. Cheapest hotdog  deals, plenty of extra activities for a variety of group types. And in the future rodeo!

reviews.title: Wonderful perfect stay. Perfect location. Beds super comfy. Will be back
reviews.text: I am giving this 5 stars because the hotel is consistent with the price charged. We used to stay at the Bellagio with the high prices and fancy priced restaurants but we have not been back since Covid and decided to come here because we had a business delivery and it was so hot in Vegas and we knew this was a one stop city unto itself. We did our business trip and then came to the hotel. Our room was fine. No carpet on floors and nice soaps and lotions. Towels fluffy. Comfortable bed and the air conditioning was cold. In a good way. We played slots a little and won more than we lost and then ate in Don Vitos Italian restaurant which was VERY reasonably priced. Use the coupons they give you when you check in. We got a free bottle of wine. Then we decided to go to the movies. They have EVERY popular movie there is. We saw Sound of Freedom still packing theaters in the fourth week.  There is so much to do here. Lots of fun slot games. LOTS of restaurants. Couldn't get into the buffet or cafe Sunday morning so went to the bar for coffee. Next time I will order room service. I will go to the oyster bar next time. Our room was very quiet. 236 in floor 2 non smoking floor. The cigarette smoke in the casino was not too awful.

reviews.title: Worst Blackjack in Vegas....
reviews.text: I can concur being an AP that they use a severe form of an offset shuffle coupled with a tight wash (in the beginning) to group like cards together forming clumps to subvert BS... which is how most people play and they know this.  1/3rd of the deck is shuffled ... the upper 1/3rd only... and bottom half isn't mixed at all... this is done 3 times. Now some dealers shuffle the entire deck 3 times... but there are other (cool off dealers) that do the shuffle which starts to clump up the deck over time thus giving the player poor hands. Doesn't matter how many players because the cards become pooled together in respective groups. If 12 10's come out... everyone pushes thus taking them out of the deck legally. If all the low cards come out with 8s and 7s mixed in... the dealer always makes a hand leaving everyone who didn't hit and those who doubled (receiving another low card) losing... this happens repeatedly. Low cards following low cards... you don't want to split either.  I would stay away.  You don't play where they purposely perform a tight wash and perpetuate card clumping via shuffling. This has been done by many casinos for years. This is why they want you to but at least  1/4 of the deck because if the dealer (and I know first hand) can group 10s and keep them at the top of the entire deck/decks... most people cut them out of the play to the bottom (thin to win motto). Try this at home you'll see what I mean if you don't believe me. Tables are overcrowded since you get a lot of locals who live right across the street (you'll see all the developments) who play and eat there. The food was good, but the place is run down and has become a vaping smokehouse.

reviews.title: Get to The Point!
reviews.text: Excellent hotel. Top quality and clean. Staff was friendly, helpful and knowledgeable. Everything from check in to leaving was pleasurable. With 11 restaurants, a bowling alley and multiple entertainment options, it’s a city in a city. No need for the strip when you can stay where everything is within one building.

reviews.title: Good place for a business stay
reviews.text: The rooms were great! We had a king size room. The room seemed bigger with just the one bed. It was extremely nice with wood flooring & not gross carpeting! Comfortable beds also. I was there on business so was in the convention center a lot of the time I was there. That space was good. We used all the space up there for different classes and events. The casino, I cannot believe Vegas allows smoking indoors. For me it was awful and I had a headache most of the time. I suffer from migraines & also had covid bad in 2021 so my lungs suffered also. The good thing about the casino was there are so many places to eat! And the Steak n Shake there was so much better than the one back home! I also liked the text to check out. All in all it is a good place to stay.

reviews.title: SHH. A shout out to Vegas' South Point Hotel and Casino
