When I call after the last super gala they say the same thing over and over that its sold out, each time I ask when they were sold out always within a week after the the super gala. So they sell to the same people over and over not giving anyone else a chance, what's even worse is they have the nerve to still post their ad for the next super gala 4 month late on their web page. I've had this problem for the last 3 years and no longer want to waste anymore time looking at Southpoint. Plaza's super bingo is by far the best there is in Las Vegas, 5 tournaments a year, great prices and deals, rooms and beds are better quality, the location alone isn't isolated like southpoint giving you lots more to do and many choices of places to eat on Fremont street. Better customer service as well.

reviews.title: Instead of being in the pool I'm writting this review ..what a shame
reviews.text: April 12th the sky is clear and it's wonderful out side .The pool is inviting. But here at South Point the pool is closed ...Bad weather they say. But the can have a man doing work on an out side building ROOF! Looks to me like the guest count is down and today they need to cut some costs. No you cant' even sit outside and read a book on this glorious day. There are other Hotels with pools open. That's our search now. Shelly the manager on duty is trying her best to explain why a guest can't sit outside and read a book at South Point. It's a sad situation. Had my review been Wednesday It would have been 3/4  stars. Read on because until today things were great. In fairness this is a great spot. You just need to understand they can and will close the pool for no reason. So don't count on it being open. Other wise this is a fine Hotel ..Buffet food is 2 stars. Beside the child that closed the pool, the staff is 5 stars. Parking staff is 5 stars. Casino staff 5 stars.. We can't weigh in on any other food options because at this point we won't invest another dime here. It's been 2 hours and Still no wind at the pool .Since I complained the man who was working on the roof is gone. Maybe the wind blew him off..

reviews.title: Beware of  the  buffet
reviews.text: This is  our 4th visit to this  hotel.  While  the  rooms are starting to  show signs of  aging they are mostly clean and  the  staff are  good. However  the buffet is  not worth your money.  You are  better off  going off site.  They leave the  food on  the  warming tables too long and  the  food  becomes unpalatable.  The  desserts are  mostly dried out and  do  not match what is displayed in the  cases.  Overall the  quality is  just not  there.....  And  it  has  become  worse over the  years.   Also we decided to  try the  Restaurant on  site on  the  right side of  the  cashiers  booth.  That  was  worse.  The  4.95 fruit cup which is  just  about  8oz apperared to be left overs from the  buffet.  I ordered a toasted English muffin, and  although  it arrived  quickly to  my  table it was  soggy and  rubbery...  The  oatmeal was  tepid at  best.  For  instant  oatmeal I would  have  expected  more...and  st  5.95 a bowl...it left  mush to be desired.

reviews.title: Excellent value
reviews.text: We ave stayed here about 6 times. It is clean and comfortable. Check in staff, especially Desiree, have been outstanding. We checked in early without an additional fee. There is no parking fee. If you don’t have a car, think about this hotel carefully. There is nothing close by. There is an annoying resort fee but we recouped some of it with the coupon booklet. There are a couple excellent restaurants: Primarily Prime and Don Vito’s.

reviews.title: Worked out well for what we needed
reviews.text: Stayed here just 2 nights for a event outside of town we attended. Checked in around 7 PM on a Wednesday night. There were 2 people checking in the line of 20 people, The counter was way understaffed for some reason. Once we get in the room was very clean and nice. Room felt a little larger than typical. We had 2 kids with us and this seemed like a good place for them a little away from the strip. We tried the pool both evenings but someone pooped in the pool and it was closed both days. Obviously a parent issue not a hotel issue. A short 10 minute drive to the strip if that's what you're looking for. The free parking was nice unlike most other locations in Vegas. I did not get to enjoy the casino or food much because I was gone most of the time. Staff was nice and helpful. Know that there are not mini-fridges in most rooms and no microwaves anywhere. I at least expected a mini-fridge.      All in all it was a nice location away from the mess of the strip. Easy access in and out, easy free parking, and kid friendly.

reviews.title: Good with a few flaws
reviews.text: My room was clean, quiet and the beds where very comfortable. I appreciate that fact the bathtub was clean. A lot of hotels think people only take showers so they don't clean the tub. This  housekeeping staff took the time to clean the tub everyday.The pool area was clean. The pool bar was excellent. The drinks had plenty of alcohol , other hotels tend to water down their drinks.  My only complaint was the hot tub with huge grates on the bottom. These grates are so high that you will stub your toes. Be careful!We were staying at the hotel for a bowling tournament. The bowling areas(2) were clean and in good order.You will smell horse poop in different areas of the hotel due to an arena inside the hotel.Now for the flaws.  The transportation to the strip and the airport was spotty. We ended up taking uber back to the airport after waiting for over 1/2 hour for a bus.There was 3 airports shuttle buses parked in the designated area but no drivers. The strip shuttle does not run between 4:30pm and 8:00 pm. The shuttle is 12 dollars a person. If you want dinner on the strip use Uber. All in all this is a great hotel if you don't want to go anywhere!

reviews.title: Good place to stay, but away from the strip
reviews.text: Stayed 3 nights at the South Point, having prebooked on booking.com. Rate was $98.10 for Sunday night & $71.10 for Monday and Tuesday nights; very reasonable. There is also a $21.00/night resort fee, including WiFi, parking was free. The room was clean & the bed comfortable. The only drawback in staying at this hotel is that it is way out of the way(beyond the airport), far form the main action on the strip. If you don't have a car, I would not recommend staying here; unless you want to stay put. There are many restaurants to choose from on the property, with plenty of bars & gambling options.

reviews.title: everything smells like cigarette smoke
reviews.text: if you enjoy the smell of cigarettes - then by all means, stay at South Pointif not, suggest you try someplace elsewhile the staff was friendly, and the rooms reasonably enough priced, there MUST be better options in LV for the non-smoker

reviews.title: Great place for families
reviews.text: We went here for our spring break with 3 year old and 6 year old child. Clean rooms, nice pool and you don't feel out of place there with kids. Excellent value and nice facilities for the price. We didn't want to leave! Has gift shop with reasonably priced everyday items (milk, alcohol, snack food), so we didn't even rent a fridge. You are about a $16 uber ride away from the strip if that is important to you. Free shuttle ride to and from airport (tip the driver).

reviews.title: Great property away from all the chaos, but still close by
reviews.text: The beds were comfortable, the rooms were clean, our breakfast at the café was delicious.  The casino was perfect for my husband's gambling.  It was a perfect location and easy to park (free) and wifi (free) to get there and back from other locations.A perfect place to stay when passing through Las Vegas.  We usually stay in Vegas as our final destination, this time however, we were headed through to Utah, but still wanted to participate in Vegas activities, but not be in all the chaos of the Strip.My only complaint is the pool was freezing, beyond freezing.  I don't know if it's because it's so soon in the season, but there was no getting use to the temperature.  We had our kids this trip, but even if we didn't, we love and enjoy pool time during the day and this pool was shockingly cold.We would have loved to enjoy bowling with our kids, but we weren't there long enough and we also left on a Tuesday, too soon to enjoy $ 5 movies....all day...that would have been a huge plus!

reviews.title: South Point - Great Stay
reviews.text: We visit South Point each year for March Madness and Football games and love it there. They have a good set up when it gets crowded and there is plenty to do there with bowling, movie theater and restaurants.  Having a more reasonable food source would be good but there is a new McDonalds straight across the street, which is perfect.  Only complaint is the resort fee when we don't use the pool(too cold) or gym (no time).  The Jacuzzi is never hot either, its just luke warm which isn't a good experience.

reviews.title: Our Favorite Hotel!!
reviews.text: We are regular visitors to Las Vegas (we go 4 or 5 times a year) and have stayed at numerous hotels.....South Point is our FAVORITE!!!  We love that is NOT right in the middle of the strip...just 5 miles south of Mandalay Bay because when you’re tired and done with the Vegas crowds, South Point is a great little retreat from it all!!  They make up for it with all the activities available to you at the hotel, as well!  For example, Bowling....sure why not!  The bowling alley is ginormous and pretty cheap (the hotel gives you coupons for free games)!  Feel like playing some arcades, yup they got one of those too!  Favorite part though, the full-size movie theater....we love taking a couple hours outta our day to watch a movie and on Tuesdays, all movies are $5.75!!!  The swimming  pool is awesome and I love the fact they have a separate pool for babies/toddlers!  There’s a cabana with drinks and food and they also have a pool store for sunscreen and such things!  As for the casino....they got some of the loosest slots in Vegas!  Even if you ain’t staying here....come and gamble!  As for food and drink,  they got lots of those to choose from too....with some the lowest prices in town, especially the buffet!  Our favorite is their Japanese restaurant located by the Steak & Shake!!  The only thing that bums me about South Point, there’s no Starbucks inside the hotel.....but they have a Seattle’s Best (which is actually owned by Starbucks)!  Best part of this hotel....LOWEST RESORT FEES IN TOWN!!!!  Also, this hotel is still old school Vegas when REWARDING their loyal customers....that’s why we’ll continue to stay here!  LOYAL LIFETIME PATRONS!!

reviews.title: Too Smokey to handle
reviews.text: The hotel and casino look awesome from outside. How can you beat the gold windows that match the mandalas bay and trump tower!?! But once you go inside it is a different story. The crowd seems much older and heavy smokers. Most of the casinos on the strip seem to have great air handlers that keep a lot of the smoke smell down. The cheap buffet that gets great reviews was below average to me and my wife. I wouldn’t recommend planning most of your vacation here unless you are a smoker or can handle the smell.

reviews.title: Business and Pleasure
reviews.text: Had an opportunity to stay at one of the older hotels in Vegas. South Point was worth the money, big rooms, plenty of good restaurants and activities for families, including movie theater, bowling and a big rodeo arena. It hosted multiple events at the same time but it did not feel overcrowded. My wife an I attended an anual convention always held at the South Point, we enjoyed ourselves.

reviews.title: Far end of the Strip but WORTH THE STAY
reviews.text: THe first thing I noticed about South point was in the booking. They do not gouge you There are no hidden fees. Booked in for a very reasonable price.  THe rooms are new. They smell great. THe Bathroom has the sink and mirror separate from the toilet and shower so Sharing a room is easy. Beds are comfortable and the Maid service is top notch. Free Wifi and valet parking. I do not gamble much. So When I drink and pay at the bar it is reasonably priced. THe food is excellent and not overly expensive. The ATM fee does not gouge you either.I am not a smoker. THe Hotel Casino allows smoking, but the ventilation is incredible. I can't say that I could smell any smoke. Smoking rooms are separately ventilated as well and I saw them changing vent filters in the rooms and they are changed before it is needed. THis hotel has a Huge Bowling alley Small Arcade and a Large Movie theatre I think at least 8 screens. THe movie prices are reasonable.I will stay here again and again

reviews.title: Ate at the Zenshin—4 stars there
reviews.text: We were passing through Las Vegas and wanted to avoid the strip. We saw the South Point, one of LV's combination casino/restaurant /entertaining/hotel complexes (including couples rooms with private sauna, steam, Jacuzzi, pool, lounge and spa services) expressed externally in gigantism. Starved for supper, we stopped, mainly for the supreme ease of parking and the realization that we would probably find an assortment of decent restaurants there. One has to walk through the casino to get to the restaurants at the back edge of the first floor—I suppose I can't argue with a business model that seems to work in LV. Once past the gauntlet, we had a good choice of eleven different places to eat—Baja Miguels, Primarily Prime Rib, Don Vito's, Silverado Steak House, Coronado Cafe, Michael's, Del-Mar Deli, Big Sur Oyster Bar, Zenshin Asian Restaurant, Steak 'n Shake and Kate's Korner Ice Cream Parlor. We chose Zenshin, whose Asian offerings seemed mainly to be Japanese. The food was fresh and flavorful, presentation was attractive (a salad came garnished with a small orchid), portions were large, the cost was  moderate considering the quantity and quality. The days of nearly or truly free meals in LV of the 1950's may be over, but it was a pleasure having supper at the Zenshin. The ratings for service, value and cleanliness are for only Zenshin, as we didn't use any of the other areas of South Point.

reviews.title: A Great  Place to Stay
reviews.text: We absolutely love the South Point. So many restaurants to choose from and delicious food in every one and at reasonable prices.  EVERYTHING at South Point is reasonably priced.  FREE parking! The rooms are clean and spacious. Employees are courteious and eager to please.  No crowds to fight with. Because of parking fees and outrageious resort fees and humongous crowds, we will NEVER stay on the strip again. Great for families with bowling and movies available and a beautiful pool area. One would never have to leave the hotel to enjoy a stay in Vegas.

reviews.title: You cant a word the management staff tells u
reviews.text: i recently booked a biz trip from vegas to chicago  based on the info i was told by management that valet parking was discounted for preferred guests   .then i found upon making a reservation the fine print said that parking offer was only for 7 days ( i needed 9  and i was staying at the hotel coming and going)  so my car would have been towed..l i would have left from Phoenix if i had gotten accurate info ...typical Vegas hustle...you cant trust a word the hotel casinos tell u

reviews.title: Nice but Location is Ok
reviews.text: The hotel is not new though there are many activities to do like the slots, gaming tables, bingos and kids amusement room etc same as any other hotel casinos. It’s somehow more or less 15 min drive from the main strip of casinos. Our room was spacious, cleaned daily by housekeepers. Silverado lounge was good to chill and have drinks. Our stay was going well except for a young woman working on the game floor serving drinks. Me my dad and my sisters were in the slots playing and called her for us to order. She looked for our ids and I said I don’t have in which I complied with going back to the room to get it. When I can back she wasn’t there so we waited for a long time and decided I’ll order straight up to the bar, showed my identification. We were drinking while playing in the slots when I saw her looking at us while passing by and just a short while a floor manager other was an American and another was a Filipina asking us our ids and the man looking like he is ready to take us out of the floor. Well anyways provided the identification a false alarm for them. Apologized and we were pissed somehow but carried on.

reviews.title: hvac conference
reviews.text: I was nice to have some options of to do will staying at the resort. my wife and I went to a movie, played bingo, watched some of the horse show, and my wife learned how to play craps with the free lessons that was offered.

reviews.title: Solid hotel with lots of activities
reviews.text: The South Point has good comfortable rooms. The hotel has many different activities that will appeal to a lot of travelers. Don't be fooled by the large amount of people who gave this hotel casino 5 stars because I suspect most of these people have never stayed in a top hotel. This is certainly NOT a top hotel. It is a good hotel. The casino floor and common areas have an overwhelming amount of unpleasant cigarette smoke. The food choices are adequate. The buffet was average. My feeling is that the clientele stay here for all the other activities. They will be pleased for sure. The hotel is good without being great, but that's OK. You could do a lot worse than the South Point. The resort fees in Las Vegas are really an insult to the traveler however.

reviews.title: Plenty of activities
reviews.text: While on Las Vegas Blvd, not really on the “strip”..rooms are nice, big and clean...check in not too bad..20 minutes. Plenty of activities, bowling, big theater, arcade, pool. Bowling is really morning and late night activity due to leagues, theater has all the popular current movies...buffet is really mediocre but price is less than strip hotels. Best is snack bar at bowling alley. He is nothing else to do in the area but hotel has a shuttle to the Strip. No problem with WiFi, but it is open access so can’t use any sites with a password...cell reception was weak..VerizonOK middle of the road Vegas hotel with comparable rooms. Old style ventilation handling system in Casino, so if a non smoker will have to wash everything when get home.
